absent: Counting and isolation behavior for shadow nodes beyond wiring of scan and count handlers.
Numeric values of eviction shift constants and storage definition for bucket orders.
Lifetime and ownership rules for shadow node list entries and their list LRU parameters.
Implementations behind handle to object translation, location resolution, chain traversal, and page chain creation.
Allocation, free, map, and compaction entry points besides the read and lookup helpers shown.
Pool creation and destruction, size class selection thresholds, and huge class configuration.
Full migration state machine beyond isolate, copy, and page substitution fragments, including completion and failure paths.
Deferred free queue mechanics and compaction worker scheduling.
Exact debugfs file operations and sequence handling behind class statistics display.
Zone, folio, and page helper semantics underlying descriptor wrappers.
Remaining aggregate guard operations such as read lock and unlock and trylock variants not shown.

findings.text: Pool service that resolves a requested byte size to the index of the matching size class through internal class selection.

Read accessor for a handle addressed object that stabilizes the owning aggregate against migration and compaction, then provides either a directly mapped view for single page residence or a caller supplied buffer filled from consecutive pages for spanning residence.
Companion release for the read accessor that drops any local mapping established for single page residence and releases the migration guard.
Observer reporting the configured huge class size associated with a pool.

Early initialization that derives timestamp and bucket sizing from total memory with headroom for later growth, creates a NUMA and memory cgroup aware reclaim object for shadow nodes, connects counting and scanning handlers, marks reclaim cost as negligible, and registers the object, cleaning up on failure.

Diagnostic formatter that walks every size class, samples per fullness and allocation counters under protection, derives page use and reclaimable estimates, and emits per class rows plus an aggregate total row.

Compact page descriptor overlay carrying status flags, recency linkage, movable operations marker, alternative next link or handle value, owning aggregate pointer, packed first object offset, and reference count.
Per size configuration holding a guard, one list per fullness band, aligned object size, object and page counts per aggregate, positional index, and usage statistics.

Allocator instance holding a name, table of size configurations, atomic page allocation total, pool statistics, reclaim object for compaction, optional accounting hooks, deferred release work, plus a read write guard and progress flag for migration safety.

Multi page aggregate with packed header distinguishing huge, fullness band, class and validity marker, live object and free slot counts, link to first page descriptor, fullness list membership, owning pool link, and a custom guarded counter for shared versus exclusive access.
Slot record that interprets the same storage as a successor position while free and as an owning handle while allocated, with dedicated caches for handles and aggregates.

Fullness bands progress from empty through intermediate utilization steps to saturated, extended by counters for total slots created and slots live, all stored in a fixed array indexed by band or counter kind.

Magic marker equals 0x58, alignment equals 8, handle width equals unsigned long width, largest allocation equals one page, smallest allocation is at least 32 bytes with a lower bound tied to aggregate size and index capacity, class spacing equals page size divided by 256, and class count equals rounded up range over spacing plus one.

Layout widths use one allocated tag bit with value one, one huge bit, four fullness bits, eight class bits, eight magic bits, page frame shift derived from address width minus frame bits, per page object bits from page shift minus five, aggregate object bits as sum with pages per aggregate bits, class encoding either class bits plus one or zero by configuration, and remaining bits for object index with masks covering each field.
Pages per aggregate encoding uses two, three, or four bits according to configured chain size, and maximum pages per aggregate equals the configured chain size.
Maximum physical memory bits equal either the architectural physical memory limit or the machine word width by configuration, with frame bits equal to that value minus page shift.
First object offset keeps only low 24 bits for byte position supporting up to 16 MiB per page, high 8 bits reserved for page typing, selected with mask 0xffffff.
Aggregate guard uses zero for unlocked and negative one for write held.
Reclaim walk for shadow nodes nests the node list lock inside the interrupt safe page tree lock.
Size class guard serializes fullness list membership, counter reads and updates, and release accounting, and must already be held when destroying an empty aggregate.
Stable reads combine pool level shared protection for handle resolution with aggregate level shared protection held across data access, releasing pool protection once the aggregate guard is acquired.
Exclusive aggregate acquisition succeeds only from the unlocked value under a spin guard, recording lock dependency state on success and leaving state unchanged on contention.

Aggregate wide page locking resolves the current head under shared protection, attempts nonblocking page acquisition, and on contention references the target, drops shared protection while waiting, then resumes, chaining through successors before finally releasing shared protection.
Descriptor overlay requires identical field offsets between generic page and compressed descriptor views, and lock, wait, reference and zone queries delegate to the underlying folio or page.

Liveness test distinguishes huge aggregates using descriptor stored handles from regular objects using embedded handles, accepts only values carrying the allocated mark, and returns the handle with mark bits cleared.
Saturation holds when live count equals class capacity and emptiness holds when live count equals zero.
Shadow reclaim accounting counts only fully disposable nodes and advertises no seek penalty.
Timestamp capacity targets the longest actionable reuse distance of about half of memory while tolerating growth to about twice initial memory through bucket order adjustment.
Reclaimable page estimate is zero unless created slots exceed live slots, otherwise wasted slots converted to whole aggregates times pages per aggregate.
Page substitution preserves chain order, carries over first object displacement and huge handle where relevant, and marks the substitute as movable.
Isolation for migration is refused when the descriptor no longer associates with an aggregate, closing a destruction race.

Aggregate destruction validates emptiness expectations, avoids sleeping acquisition with a deferred fallback on contention, detaches from fullness tracking on success, and updates allocation and accounting totals.

Compaction drains sparsely populated aggregates into densely populated ones, detaching both ends from tracking during movement and reinserting them according to recomputed fullness, halting when the sink saturates or the source empties.

Fixed size object relocation tolerates page splits in source and destination by mapping the active pages locally and advancing through the smaller remaining extent until the whole object is transferred, respecting required unmap ordering across page crossings.
Release context cannot sleep, so it must use nonblocking aggregate acquisition and defer work when acquisition fails rather than waiting on page locks.
Nested local mappings impose reverse order release, so crossing a source page boundary requires releasing the destination mapping first.
Packed displacement must be reached through helpers rather than direct field use, and huge handling assumes operation on the leading descriptor.

Accounting presence is configuration dependent: with support, a top level directory and per pool class file are created with warnings when unavailable and removed on teardown; without support, all accounting hooks do nothing.
One build configuration defines deferred release initialization as having no effect.
Logging output carries a module derived prefix and the descriptor header is protected by an inclusion guard.
